run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T22:16:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by the otel-demo/product-catalog workload becoming unstartable. The product-catalog Deployment's pod template now runs container command ["invalid-command"] with the unchanged image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog; the new ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf (created 2026-11-17T22:14:15Z) replaced the previous command-less ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc, and its pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l cannot start (StartError, exit code 128, 'exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH', CrashLoopBackOff, 5 restarts). The product-catalog Service therefore has only notReadyAddresses and the Deployment reports Available=False / MinimumReplicasUnavailable. Frontend error spans were exactly 0 from the sampled baseline start (21:56) through the 22:15:00 evaluation, first became non-zero in the interval ending 22:16:00 (516.67 per 5m), and reached ~5453-7119 per 5m from 22:20 onward, i.e. ~58% of its spans erroring. Frontend error spans are concentrated on its product-catalog path (grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, GET /api/products/{productId}, executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]), and the other failing services fail on their own product-catalog client calls (recommendation '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts', checkout 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct'), while no other Deployment in the cluster carries the invalid-command setting and all flagd fault flags are off. Who applied the template change is not visible (change_history is not integrated).

claims.text: otel-demo/product-catalog Deployment's container command is ["invalid-command"] with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog; a cluster-wide scan found this to be the only Deployment whose container command is invalid-command.

The pair of ReplicaSets shows this was a configuration-only template change: product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 2026-11-17T21:44:14Z, replicas 0) has command null, while product-catalog-fcf7564cf (created 2026-11-17T22:14:15Z, replicas 1) has command ["invalid-command"] and the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog.

Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l (owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf) is running but its product-catalog container is not ready, restartCount 5, state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff, and lastState terminated reason StartError exitCode 128 with message 'failed to create containerd task: ... exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH'.

otel-demo events record the product-catalog rollout and its failure: Deployment product-catalog ScalingReplicaSet events scaled down product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc 1->0 and product-catalog-fcf7564cf 1->0 at 22:14:24Z and scaled up product-catalog-fcf7564cf 0->1 at 22:14:32Z, ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf SuccessfulCreate/Delete events, and Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l Failed/BackOff events carrying 'exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH'.

Deployment product-catalog (generation 4, spec.replicas 1) reports status replicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, condition Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ('Deployment does not have minimum availability.').

The product-catalog Service (clusterIP 100.64.32.100, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog) has an Endpoints object with only notReadyAddresses pointing at pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l (100.96.2.148) and no ready addresses.

Frontend error-status spans had a zero baseline (0 per 5m at every evaluation from 21:56:00 through 22:15:00), first became non-zero at the 22:16:00 evaluation (516.67 per 5m, covering 22:11-22:16), then rose to 2358.87 / 3959.17 / 5534.42 / 6648.89 per 5m at 22:17-22:20 and stayed at 6598.73-7118.88 through 22:24 and 5452.94 for 22:20-22:25.

At 22:25:00 the frontend's error spans were 57.6% of its spans (STATUS_CODE_ERROR fraction 0.5763 vs 0 at 22:15:00), and its non-error UNSET span volume fell from ~13606 per 5m at 22:15 to ~4009-5332 per 5m after 22:20.

Frontend error spans over 22:20-22:25 sit on its product-catalog call path: grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 1029.04, GET /api/products/{productId} 1029.04, executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId] 1029.04, GET 1233.37, plus grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations 204.33 and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 129.25.
product-catalog stopped emitting spans: its 5-minute span increase fell from ~3281.11 at 22:15:00 to 2563.33 / 1756.67 / 962.22 / 102.22 at 22:16-22:19 and 0 from 22:20:00 onward.

Error spans by service over 22:20-22:25: frontend 5452.94, frontend-proxy 2780.63, recommendation 423.43, checkout 260.95, ad 1.23, and 0 for accounting, fraud-detection and payment; recommendation's errors are on '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' and 'get_product_list' (211.72 each), checkout's on 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (130.48 each), and frontend-proxy's on 'ingress' (1392.16) and 'router frontend egress' (1388.47).

The frontend pod itself was not crashing or restarting: frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 is Running with the frontend container ready, restartCount 0, started at 2026-11-17T21:44:16Z, and its error spans are attributed to downstream product-catalog (and product-catalog-dependent recommendation/checkout) calls rather than to frontend restarts.

No fault-injection feature flag is engaged: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json), including productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, adFailure, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, has defaultVariant "off" and value false/0.

Feature-flag-driven fault injection through flagd (e.g. productCatalogFailure) is rejected: all flagd flags read as defaultVariant "off", and the failure mechanism visible on product-catalog is a container start error from the Deployment's own command, not a runtime flag decision.

NetworkPolicy blocking or ResourceQuota exhaustion as the cause of frontend->product-catalog failures is rejected: the otel-demo namespace contains no networkpolicy objects and no resourcequota objects, and the product-catalog Service has no ready endpoints because its only pod cannot start.

Restore a valid startup command on Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog (revert the pod-template change that set command ["invalid-command"]) and confirm a product-catalog pod reaches Ready so the Service regains ready endpoints; then re-check frontend error-rate and product-catalog span volume.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so the identity of the actor or pipeline that changed the product-catalog pod template to command ["invalid-command"] at ~22:14Z could not be observed, and the exact time the setting was written (only its effects: ReplicaSet creation 22:14:15Z, first pod failure 22:14:20Z, Deployment condition lastUpdateTime 22:14:24Z) is unknown.

Jaeger returned spans only up to 2026-11-17T21:59:33Z (source_end_at) for the frontend search, so no error trace or error span detail exists in the trace store for the 22:16-22:25Z error window; tag searches for error=true and otel.status_code="ERROR" on frontend returned no traces, so the exact gRPC error code/message of the failing calls is unverified (error attribution rests on metric span-name counts).

Pod logs were not obtainable: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 (with and without an error filter, and for the whole authorized window) and for product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l returned 0 lines (no_data), so frontend application error text and any product-catalog startup output are unknown; the product-catalog container never started, so it likely wrote nothing.

kube-state-metrics series for kube_deployment_status_replicas_available, kube_pod_container_info and kube_pod_owner returned no data in this target, so replica-availability history and an image_id/digest comparison between the old and new product-catalog ReplicaSets are unavailable; image equality is supported only by the identical image strings in both ReplicaSet templates.

list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name RequestErrorRate (no_data, not citable), so the exact PromQL expression and evaluation interval behind the alert's reported value of 16.8667 are unverified.
The ad service shows 1.23 error spans over 22:20-22:25; this was not investigated further and is not tied to the product-catalog failure.

fraud-detection pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-8bpr4 was Created/Started at 22:04:18Z, before the error onset, and fraud-detection had 0 error spans over 22:20-22:25; its restart is not explained by the evidence gathered.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | select(.metadata.name=="flagd-config") | .data["demo.flagd.json"]

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
